findings.description: A long-lived AWS access key ID and secret access key are embedded in cleartext in the Lambda environment variables block, committing credentials to source control and Terraform state and exposing them to anyone with lambda:GetFunctionConfiguration or repository/state read access.

No kms_key_arn is set, so the environment variables holding these secrets are protected only by the default AWS-managed key, with no customer-managed key policy boundary or separate audit trail restricting who can decrypt them.
The function targets nodejs12.x, which is past end of life and no longer receives security patches from AWS, leaving known vulnerabilities in the execution environment unaddressed.

No vpc_config is defined, so the function runs outside any customer VPC with unrestricted outbound internet egress and no security group or subnet boundary, easing exfiltration of the embedded credentials if the function is compromised.
The trust policy allows lambda.amazonaws.com to assume the role with no aws:SourceAccount or aws:SourceArn condition, weakening the trust boundary against cross-account confused-deputy abuse.
